_readme: What the open-access EMC literature says about how its patients die. Every row is a PATIENT or reported patient group, never a sentence, and every quote has been asserted against the retrieval artifact verbatim before this file was written. Nothing here is a rate, an incidence or a prognosis: it is a description of what a body of case reports and small series chose to record, in a disease too rare for anything better to exist.

corpus.⚠_inclusion_note: Only 34 of the 162 papers carrying a death sentence are about EMC. The rest match the enumeration because EMC appears in a differential diagnosis or a citation, and their deaths belong to other diseases' patients. Every count below is restricted to the 34.

headline.⭐_the_finding: The published record of this disease mostly does not say how its patients died. That is not a gap in this table -- it is the result. A treatment portfolio aimed at preventing a specific event cannot describe the event it is aimed at.

competing_and_second_malignancy.⭐_reading: Deaths from a competing cause or a second cancer are the largest identifiable mechanism category in this corpus. They recur across independent case series, and they converge with the registry cause-split computed separately in emc-mortality-decomposition.json. ⚠ Case reports over-select the notable, so this is not an incidence -- but the direction agrees with the registry, which is not a case-report artifact.

respiratory.⛔_the_premise_this_does_not_support: Respiratory failure from progressive pulmonary metastases is present in this corpus and is NOT its dominant named mechanism. One of the three respiratory deaths followed a tumour-embolic ischaemic stroke rather than pulmonary tumour burden. Lung is unambiguously EMC's dominant metastatic SITE; that is a different claim from lung failure being its dominant mode of death, and this corpus does not establish the second.

aggregate_cause_splits.quote: Of the 128 patients who did not receive (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy, 88 (68.8%) were tumor-free survivors, 28 (21.9%) survived with tumors, eight (6.3%) died from tumors, and four (3.1%) died from other causes.
aggregate_cause_splits.note: ⚠ Overlaps the localised stratum already used in emc-mortality-decomposition-inputs.json. Recorded for completeness and EXCLUDED from any pooled total, because pooling overlapping strata from one registry double-counts patients.

aggregate_cause_splits.quote: Among the 16 patients who received advanced-stage chemotherapy, one (6.3%) survived tumor-free, nine (56.3%) survived with tumors, five (31.3%) died of the tumors, and one (6.3%) died of other causes.
aggregate_cause_splits.note: Also overlapping; excluded from pooling for the same reason.

aggregate_cause_splits.quote: Among the 13 patients who did not receive advanced-stage chemotherapy, nine (69.2%) survived with tumors, and four (30.8%) died of tumors.

prognostic_findings.quote: The results showed that the risk factors for death due to tumors were tumor location on the trunk (odds ratio (OR) 8.52 [95% CI: 1.50–48.36]; p = 0.016) and the occurrence of distant metastasis (OR 26.26 [95% CI: 2.99–231.04]; p = 0.003; Table S1 ).
prognostic_findings.corroborating_quote: No association was found between local recurrence and tumor mortality.
prognostic_findings.note: ⭐ Directly relevant to what a treatment should target. EMC's much-quoted 30-50% local recurrence rate is NOT associated with dying of the disease in this registry's multivariate model; distant metastasis is, with a very wide confidence interval on a small event count.

individual_events.label: respiratory_failure
individual_events.quote: Here, we present a case which initially demonstrated a typical indolent course of EMC, but rapidly progressed after the marginal resection and eventually died of pulmonary failure.
individual_events.note: The clearest respiratory death in the corpus. The same patient is described again in the paper's discussion as dying of respiratory failure; both sentences are one patient and are counted once.

individual_events.label: respiratory_failure
individual_events.quote: One patient died due to lung metastases.
individual_events.note: Attributed to lung metastases as the cause of death. ⚠ Read as a respiratory death on the paper's own attribution; it does not name the physiological terminal event, so this is the weaker of the two respiratory rows.

individual_events.label: respiratory_failure
individual_events.quote: Despite slight neurological recovery, the patient died of respiratory failure on the 15th day after onset.
individual_events.note: ⚠ Respiratory failure, but by an unusual route: EMC tumour emboli caused an acute ischaemic stroke treated by thrombectomy, and death followed 15 days later. Counted as respiratory because that is what the paper names, but the initiating event was embolic, not pulmonary tumour burden. A mechanism table that hid this would misrepresent it.

individual_events.label: locoregional_complication
individual_events.quote: The patient received adjuvant radiotherapy but died after 1 year of follow-up due to complications of locoregional tumor dissemination to the skull base.
individual_events.note: Paediatric masticator-space EMC with a compromised superior margin. Four sentences, one patient. Death from local dissemination at an anatomically unforgiving site, not from distant metastasis.

individual_events.label: locoregional_complication
individual_events.quote: Only 1 out of the 11 patients who underwent PR died from local recurrence and spinal metastasis of primary intracranial EMC at 36 mo after surgery[ 9 ].
individual_events.note: Primary intracranial EMC, a rare presentation where local control governs outcome.

individual_events.label: competing_non_cancer
individual_events.quote: In our research of the 16 primary intracranial EMC cases available in the literature, 3 did not have any information on the prognosis of patients, and in 2 cases, the patients died from non-EMC-related factors after surgery.
individual_events.note: Two of sixteen collected intracranial cases died of causes the reviewers judged unrelated to EMC. ⚠ The paper does not name those causes, so the label records what it asserts and no more.

individual_events.label: emc_progressive_disease
individual_events.quote: The patient subsequently underwent radiation to the brain and failed systemic treatment with chemotherapy and immunotherapy, with the development of further metastases ultimately resulting in death.
individual_events.note: Multi-site progression including brain metastases. No single terminal mechanism named.

individual_events.label: visceral_metastasis_complication
individual_events.quote: Due to persistent anemia and gastrointestinal bleeding, the patient case was presented to the multidisciplinary tumor board, and it was recommended to proceed with palliative small bowel tumor resection.
individual_events.note: ⚠ Not a death sentence. Small-bowel metastasis causing obstruction and bleeding, retained because it documents a mechanism of harm from non-pulmonary visceral metastasis that no other row carries. Counted in the mechanism table only as a complication, never as a death.

individual_events.label: treatment_related
individual_events.quote: Of the remaining five patients, two showed tumor recurrences and two died due to postoperative complications 2 , 14 , 15 , 17) .
individual_events.note: Intracranial EMC literature review. Two postoperative deaths -- treatment-caused, in a series where the operation is at the skull base.

individual_events.label: second_malignancy
individual_events.quote: The patient was followed for 126 months, after which he died from complications of unresectable colon cancer.
individual_events.note: ⭐ The single most informative row in the corpus. Metastatic EMC, alive at 126 months, dead of an unrelated colon cancer. A patient who lived more than a decade with metastatic sarcoma and was killed by a different disease.

individual_events.label: second_malignancy
individual_events.quote: Two patients with EMC died during follow-up from concurrent malignancies ( Table 2 ).
individual_events.note: The same two patients are described again as dying 'from concurrent malignancies within the first few months after diagnosis'. One event, counted once.

individual_events.label: mechanism_unstated
individual_events.quote: Both patients that presented with metastatic disease to the lungs died within 17 months ( Table 2 ).
individual_events.note: Lung-metastatic at presentation, dead within 17 months, no mechanism given. ⚠ It is tempting to read these as respiratory deaths and the paper does not say so.

individual_events.label: mixed_see_note
individual_events.quote: Three patients died 9 months (the patient with lung and skin metastasis later developed congestive heart disease), 10 months (the patient with hepatic metastasis), and 9.5 years (cerebral hemorrhage but no tumor recurrence) following the primary diagnosis ( Tab.
individual_events.note: One sentence, three patients, three different stories: congestive heart disease in a patient with lung and skin metastases (attribution genuinely ambiguous), hepatic metastasis (EMC progression), and cerebral haemorrhage explicitly WITHOUT tumour recurrence at 9.5 years (a competing death). Split in the tally as 1 ambiguous, 1 visceral_metastasis_complication, 1 competing_non_cancer.

individual_events.label: mechanism_unstated
individual_events.quote: Two patients died of disease 8 months after the initial diagnosis.
individual_events.note: 'Died of disease' -- the canonical form of the corpus's dominant non-answer.

individual_events.label: mechanism_unstated
individual_events.quote: Three patients died during the time-frame of the study, 1 was lost to follow up, and 9 are still alive.
individual_events.note: Seven sentences describing the same three deaths, none naming a mechanism. The clearest single illustration of why sentence counting would have been wrong.

individual_events.label: emc_progressive_disease
individual_events.quote: While recurrence developed in 5 (38.5%) of the patients during follow-up, lung metastasis (46.2%) was detected in 6 patients, and 7 patients (53.8%) died due to the disease and complications related to the disease.
individual_events.note: Seven deaths attributed to disease and its complications collectively. No per-patient mechanism, so this cannot enter a mechanism table -- only a cause-attribution one.

individual_events.label: mechanism_unstated
individual_events.quote: With a median follow-up time of 72 months, 20 patients have died.
individual_events.note: The largest single block of deaths in the corpus, and all-cause: the paper does not split them by cause at all.

individual_events.label: mechanism_unstated
individual_events.quote: The patient consequently deteriorated clinically and was referred for palliative radiation and transitioned to supportive care.
individual_events.note: Transition to supportive care recorded; the death itself and its mechanism are not described.

limits: A convenience sample: open-access full text only, 328 of 600 enumerated papers retrieved, and non-open-access series are systematically older and larger.

Case reports are written because a case was notable, so unusual terminal events are over-represented and ordinary ones under-represented. This biases AGAINST the indolent, competing-cause picture the tally nevertheless shows.
Counts are of reported patients, not of a defined population, so no denominator exists and no rate can be computed from this table.
A label records what a paper asserted, never an independent adjudication. Where a paper called a death unrelated to EMC, that is the paper's judgement and its instrument is unknown.
